recognize_zh: 大量小而圓、深染且缺乏中央淡染區的球形紅血球（spherocytes），中央有一顆有核紅血球（nucleated RBC），另可見少數偏大、偏藍灰的多染性紅血球（polychromasia），符合遺傳性球形紅血球症溶血恢復期的表現。
features: Numerous spherocytes: small, round, densely stained red cells lacking central pallor
Mixed population with normal discocytes showing central pallor
Single nucleated red cell with condensed round nucleus and small rim of cytoplasm
Scattered larger bluish-gray polychromatophilic red cells
Adequate platelets; partial neutrophil at lower right edge
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous spherocytes, which are small, round and hyperchromatic without central pallor, admixed with normal discocytes. Scattered larger polychromatophilic red cells are present, and a single nucleated red blood cell is seen in the center of the field, indicating an active marrow erythroid response. Red cell fragments and agglutinates are not prominent, and platelets appear adequate. In the appropriate clinical context (recovery from parvovirus B19 infection), findings are consistent with hereditary spherocytosis.

ddx.vs: Warm AIHA can show identical spherocytes with polychromasia, so a positive direct antiglobulin test (versus negative in HS) and family history/EMA binding are required to separate them.

ddx.dx: ABO hemolytic disease of the newborn
ddx.vs: Neonatal ABO incompatibility produces microspherocytes with a positive DAT in an infant of an O mother, rather than a chronic familial pattern.
MAHA shows schistocytes (helmet cells, triangular fragments) and thrombocytopenia rather than a predominance of round intact spherocytes.
HPP has microspherocytes plus bizarre budding fragments and elliptocytes with a very low MCV, which are not present here.
